summary: A fire tower built by 1925 on Rich Mountain in Randolph County, sold and moved to Snowshoe Mountain ski resort in 1999, restored in 2000 and now used as an attraction.

access.note: On privately owned Snowshoe Mountain ski-resort land; the 2021 visit found directions to the tower signed

visit.trail_note: Tower sits at the Snowshoe Mountain ski resort; check with the resort before going. Do not climb without permission.

events.note: Built by 1925 as the Rich Mountain fire tower in Randolph County; administered by the West Virginia Division of Forestry
Removed from Rich Mountain and sold to Snowshoe Mountain, Inc. for one dollar, per one history page
Dismantled and moved to the Snowshoe ski resort in Pocahontas County
Reconditioned to original specifications, painted and reassembled at Snowshoe
NHLR visit report, June 25, 2021: good condition, stairs and wood OK, directions to tower signed
Photo of footings at the original Randolph County site, July 2022

corrections.current: 1999 built ('Built' field on NHLR detail page)
corrections.proposed: 1925 built (by 1925, Rich Mountain, Randolph County); 1999 relocated to Snowshoe Mountain
corrections.why: The NHLR 'Built' field gives 1999, which is the year the tower was moved. The FFLOS register gives Built by 1925 for the Randolph County tower and records its removal in 1999.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says Built 1999; FFLOS says Built by 1925 and Removed 1999. The 1925 build date is kept, and 1999 is recorded as the relocation.

FFLOS names the West Virginia Division of Forestry as administrator of the Randolph County tower before 1999. One history page says the Department of Natural Resources sold it for one dollar. The NHLR names Snowshoe Mountain, Inc. as administrator now, so facts.agency uses Snowshoe Mountain, Inc.

notes_for_editor: Build date 'by 1925' comes from the FFLOS Randolph County record; NHLR's Built 1999 is the relocation year. The record's events list 1999 as built and should be corrected. A WBOY search snippet places the tower 'on top of Cheat Ridge' in Pocahontas County; the page was not read, so the Snowshoe Mountain location rests on NHLR. The 80-foot height is from one history page only. Access: private resort ground; no climbing.
